long_biography.plain_text:
Limestone Asset Management grew from Ibrahim Al-Rashid's decision to build a dedicated North American property platform with Orion Real Estate Group. He founded the Miami company in 2010 and focused its acquisitions on commercial assets whose locations, tenants and long leases could support durable value. The portfolio expanded from individual restaurant and retail sites to shopping centres, offices and mixed-use properties.

Al-Rashid's approach combines patient ownership with selective larger transactions. Limestone assembled portfolios of nationally tenanted properties, entered additional Florida markets and added residential development to its remit. A major acquisition brought a large Pinecrest retail centre into the joint venture, extending the scale of a platform previously reported at about $200 million in assets. Al-Rashid remains chairman, maintaining founder oversight of the firm's continuing acquisition strategy.

uncertainties.detail: Al-Rashid demonstrably founded and expanded Limestone, while reliable reporting identifies his father as a Saudi billionaire. No reviewed source proves a transfer of the Limestone stake, a specific inheritance or independently sourced launch capital. Self-made — advantaged start therefore captures a founder-built company formed from a materially privileged platform without asserting an undocumented inheritance.

Sources describe Limestone as Al-Rashid's founded company and a joint venture with Orion, but do not publish his exact equity percentage. Founder is strongly supported as his relationship to the business; company portfolio values are not presented as his personal net worth.

Florida filings use both Ibrahim Al-Rashid and Ibrahim N. Al-Rashid, while a separate UK shareholder filing expands the middle name to Nasser. The latter does not provide enough identity context to support a middle-name proposal. The immutable 1984 birth year is retained; exact birth day, month, place and country remain unresolved.

The immutable record gives Saudi Arabian nationality and United States residence, both consistent with reliable profiles of this Miami-based son of a Saudi businessman. Public descriptions do not establish United States citizenship or another nationality, so no secondary nationality is proposed.

No personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website attributable above the identity threshold was found. A same-name Miami LinkedIn belongs to a Kuwaiti designer, and the former Orion affiliates page now returns a not-found response, so no social or Company Website is proposed.

Current vessel facts were used only to resolve the exact identity and do not appear in either biography. Personal residences, family circumstances, political activity, allegations, controversy, private purchases and transient deal forecasts were excluded. Nothing has been compiled or applied.
